question: Does the conditional five-second temporal hierarchy contain a concrete high-concentration capture run that makes the split hazard intelligible without promoting adjacency to scene truth?
terminal_objective: Find and freeze the strongest exact microcase behind the aggregate temporal-sensitivity result.
method: Verify the Stage 10O manifest identity, rank its five-second conditional clusters by unique reconstructed actions and then product rows, and freeze the largest cluster's product, capture, action, byte, time-span, camera, activity, target, and hypothetical 80/20 crossing values.
authority: Private local metadata analysis only. No pixels, model training, publication, outreach, semantic scene claim, label-correctness claim, observed leakage, performance effect, or priority claim.
claim_ceiling: Stage 10P may establish the exact concentration of the largest conditional five-second same-camera cluster in the verified cohort and its expected crossing under hypothetical independent action assignment. It cannot call that cluster a semantic scene or independent sample, validate activity or target correctness, claim observed leakage or a performance effect, generalize the largest cluster to the archive, infer image content or similarity, or claim global novelty or priority.

next_step_logic.if_the_cluster_verifies: Use the Sunset microcase to make the hierarchy concrete, always paired with the conditional-threshold and nonsemantic-label caveats.
next_step_logic.if_a_real_model_task_uses_these_products: Inspect its actual split and task dependence before computing observed overlap or performance effects.
next_step_logic.if_the_manifest_changes: Re-rank all five-second clusters before reusing the microcase.
next_step_logic.recheck_trigger: A revised relationship manifest, real model task, image-similarity oracle, or authoritative capture-episode identifier.
